summary: On 12 June 2026, Anthropic said the U.S. government had ordered it to suspend Fable 5 and Mythos 5 access for foreign nationals, including its own foreign-national employees. Anthropic said it would disable both models for all customers to comply. It disputed the government’s apparent concern about a possible narrow jailbreak and said other Anthropic models would remain available. Later reporting described the restriction being lifted. The order itself and the government’s technical evidence are not preserved in this record.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: The 0.6.7 recognition conditions for Jurisdiction-Bounded Infrastructure Authority are supported by Anthropic’s contemporaneous account: a U.S. sovereign restriction named foreign nationals inside and outside the country, while the globally used model service disabled the affected models for all customers. The directive’s narrower actor scope was not preserved in the provider-wide access effect. Classification does not adjudicate the order’s legality or Anthropic’s technical alternatives. Infrastructure–Governance Authority Separation is not separately asserted because the record does not show dependency being used as an authority basis; Infrastructural Access Choice Integrity lacks an extracted concession or leverage demand.

assessment_boundaries: The government directive and underlying technical demonstration are not directly available; its scope is recorded from Anthropic’s contemporaneous statement.
Anthropic’s description of the jailbreak and its proportionality objection are interested-party positions, not independent findings.
The U.S. directive was described as applying to foreign nationals inside and outside the United States; this record does not determine its legal reach or validity.
The provider-wide loss of both models exceeded the named foreign-national cohort, but the record does not disclose whether narrower access segregation was feasible or legally sufficient.
S3 service interruption is based on the announced all-customer disablement and subsequent reported restoration; customer-specific downstream losses are not inferred.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Anthropic’s 12 June statement says a U.S. export-control directive barred access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 by foreign nationals inside and outside the United States, including its own affected employees. Anthropic said it had to disable both models for all customers to comply, while other models remained available. The public statement was directly reviewed; the directive itself and its technical evidence were not. Later reporting describes the restriction being lifted. The record supports a provider-wide service interruption and a restriction propagated beyond the directive’s named foreign-national cohort, without establishing the legal validity or technical proportionality of the order.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The source identifies a concrete infrastructure authority projection. The government directive targeted foreign nationals, including people outside the United States; Anthropic then removed Fable 5 and Mythos 5 from all customers to comply. A sovereign access restriction thus became a broader rule of availability through a globally relied-upon provider. VIGIL maps this operational scope expansion to Jurisdiction-Bounded Infrastructure Authority at medium confidence. The classification concerns the infrastructure-mediated effect on users beyond the targeted cohort, not a finding that the government lacked legal power over foreign nationals, that Anthropic acted unlawfully, or that a less restrictive technical implementation was immediately feasible. The undisclosed order and compliance architecture limit stronger causal and legal conclusions.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: A host nation’s control over a model provider can become access control for people outside the named regulatory cohort when globally shared infrastructure has no narrower way to apply the order. The governing invariant is to preserve the issuing authority, affected users, jurisdiction, duration and independent basis for any wider restriction. Provider-wide disablement should be visible as a distinct implementation decision with review and restoration paths.
